evals.name: build-invite-form-from-scratch
evals.prompt: We're adding a team invite flow to our React app (TypeScript, Vite, react-hook-form + zod already installed). Can you build the invite form? It needs an email field, a role dropdown with member/admin where member is the default, and an optional message textarea capped at 500 chars. The parent page owns the mutation - it POSTs to /api/invites - so the form itself shouldn't do the fetch. Put it under src/features/team/. Show me the files.
evals.expected_output: A single colocated folder (e.g. src/features/team/InviteMemberForm/) containing InviteMemberForm.tsx, useInviteMemberForm.ts and invite-member-form.schema.ts. Schema uses z.input/z.output (never z.infer), hook uses useForm<Input, unknown, Output> with zodResolver and mode 'onTouched', onSubmit arrives as a prop typed to the Output type, submit button is type=submit and is not disabled by validity.
assertions: Schema lives in its own file suffixed .schema.ts
Schema filename is kebab-case
Schema const is camelCase ending in `Schema`
z.infer is not used
Both z.input<> and z.output<> are used
Types named ...FormInput / ...FormOutput
mode: 'onTouched' is set
zodResolver is wired up
useForm uses all three generics <Input, Context, Output>
useForm call is isolated in a use…Form.ts hook file
Hook accepts defaultValues
Submission is wired on the <form> element via handleSubmit
No gratuitous id on the form element (no outside submit button)
Submit button declares type="submit"
Submit is not wired through the button's onClick
Button is not disabled by validity or dirtiness
onSubmit arrives as a typed prop
Form component itself does not perform the network call
watch / formState are never destructured from useForm or useFormContext
Uses useFormState and/or useWatch
Hook file exports no type aliases (they belong in a .types.ts)
No .types.ts file unless a field component imports from it
No FormProvider (not needed at this depth)
Component, hook and schema are colocated in one folder
Role field defaults to 'member'
Message is optional and capped at 500

evals.name: extend-form-with-dependent-field
evals.prompt: Here's our existing ShippingAddressForm. I need to add a country select and a state/province select where the states list depends on which country is picked (and the state field should disappear entirely for countries that don't have states). Assume there's a useStates(countryCode) hook available that returns { data }. Add it to the form.
evals.expected_output: Country stays inline (simple select), but the dependent state field is extracted into its own component in the same folder, named ShippingAddressFormStateField.tsx, receiving control as a prop (typed via the exported ShippingAddressFormControl alias) and reading the country with useWatch({ control, name: 'country' }) rather than lifting a watch into the parent. Schema updated in the existing .schema.ts file.

evals.name: fix-nonconforming-form
evals.prompt: This ProfileSettingsForm was written by someone who just left and it doesn't match how we do forms here. Can you refactor it to follow our conventions? Don't change what the form actually does for the user.
evals.expected_output: Split into a ProfileSettingsForm/ folder with component + hook + profile-settings-form.schema.ts. z.infer replaced with z.input/z.output, mode switched to onTouched, FormProvider removed (no nested consumers justify it), destructured watch/formState replaced with useWatch/useFormState, the bare <div> becomes a <form> with an id and onSubmit={handleSubmit(...)} instead of the button's onClick, the disabled={!isValid || !isDirty} guard removed so only isSubmitting can lock the button, and the fetch moved out to an onSubmit prop.
